## mcrl host create

Register a host.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host create --name <name> [flags]

Aliases:
  create, new

Register a host without mackerel-agent, for example to post metrics or check
results for something that cannot run the agent. The output is the
registered host (fetched again after registration).

"meta" defaults to {}. Interfaces and the full meta can be given with -f.

API: POST /api/v0/hosts
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl host create --name router-1 --role network:router --custom-identifier router-1.example.com
  mcrl host create --name batch-1 --check backup --check 'nightly=daily batch' --memo 'no agent'

Flags:
      --check stringArray          check monitor name the host reports, as name or name=memo (repeatable; replaces the list)
      --custom-identifier string   custom identifier ("" clears it)
      --display-name string        display name
  -f, --file string                JSON or YAML file in the API's format ("-" for stdin); flags override its fields
      --memo string                memo
      --name string                host name
      --no-refetch[=true|false]    print the API response ({"success": true}) instead of fetching the updated resource
      --role stringArray           role as <service>:<role> (repeatable; missing services and roles are created)
```

## mcrl host edit

Edit a host's information in $EDITOR.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host edit <host>

Open the host's updatable fields (name, displayName, customIdentifier, memo,
meta, interfaces) as YAML in $VISUAL or $EDITOR, then show the changes and
send them after confirmation. Roles are changed with "mcrl host role".

The host is given by ID, exact name, or "cid:<custom identifier>".
A name that looks like an ID can be forced with the "name:" prefix.

API: GET /api/v0/hosts/<id>, PUT /api/v0/hosts/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl host edit web-1
  EDITOR='code --wait' mcrl host edit cid:router-1.example.com
```

## mcrl host get

Show a host.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host get <host>

Aliases:
  get, show

Show a host.

The host is given by ID, exact name, or "cid:<custom identifier>".
A name that looks like an ID can be forced with the "name:" prefix.

API: GET /api/v0/hosts/<id>, GET /api/v0/hosts?name=, GET /api/v0/hosts-by-custom-identifier/<cid>
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl host get web-1
  mcrl host get cid:i-0123456789abcdef0
  mcrl host get exampleHst1 --jq '.roles'
```

## mcrl host list

List hosts.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host list [flags]

Aliases:
  list, ls

List hosts.

Without --status, the API returns working and standby hosts. Use
"--status all" for every status. Retired hosts are never listed.
--name matches the host name exactly and case-sensitively.

API: GET /api/v0/hosts
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl host list
  mcrl host list --service web --role app --status all
  mcrl host list --status poweroff --jq '.[].id'

Flags:
      --custom-identifier string   only the host with this custom identifier
      --name string                only hosts with this exact name
      --role stringArray           only hosts with this role of --service (repeatable)
      --service string             only hosts in this service
      --status stringArray         only hosts in this status: working, standby, maintenance, poweroff or all (repeatable)
```

## mcrl host monitor-status

Show the status of each monitor on a host.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host monitor-status <host> [flags]

Show the status of each monitor that targets a host.

--expand adds "_expanded": {"monitor": {"name", "type"}} to each entry.

The host is given by ID, exact name, or "cid:<custom identifier>".
A name that looks like an ID can be forced with the "name:" prefix.

API: GET /api/v0/hosts/<id>/monitored-statuses, GET /api/v0/monitors (--expand)
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl host monitor-status web-1
  mcrl host monitor-status web-1 --expand --jq '.[] | select(.status != "OK") | ._expanded.monitor.name'

Flags:
      --expand[=true|false]   add monitor names under _expanded
```

## mcrl host retire

Retire hosts.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host retire <host>... [flags]

Retire hosts. Retired hosts stop being monitored and cannot be restored.

Pass "-" to read hosts from stdin, one per line. Several hosts are retired
30 at a time with the bulk API. The output is an array of the retired hosts.

The host is given by ID, exact name, or "cid:<custom identifier>".
A name that looks like an ID can be forced with the "name:" prefix.

API: POST /api/v0/hosts/<id>/retire, POST /api/v0/hosts/bulk-retire
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl host retire web-old-1
  mcrl host list --status poweroff --jq '.[].id' | mcrl host retire --yes -

Flags:
      --no-refetch[=true|false]   print the API response ({"success": true}) instead of fetching the updated resource
```

## mcrl host role add

Add roles to a host.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host role add <host> <service:role>... [flags]

Add roles to a host.

Roles are given as "<service>:<role>". The API creates services and roles
that do not exist yet.

The host is given by ID, exact name, or "cid:<custom identifier>".
A name that looks like an ID can be forced with the "name:" prefix.

API: PUT /api/v0/hosts/<id>/role-fullnames
API key permission: Write

Examples:
  mcrl host role add web-1 web:app
  mcrl host role add web-1 web:app web:batch

Flags:
      --no-refetch[=true|false]   print the API response ({"success": true}) instead of fetching the updated resource
```

## mcrl host status

Change the status of hosts.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host status <status> <host>... [flags]

Change the status of hosts to working, standby, maintenance or poweroff.

Pass "-" to read hosts from stdin, one per line. Several hosts are updated
30 at a time with the bulk API. The output is an array of the updated hosts.

The host is given by ID, exact name, or "cid:<custom identifier>".
A name that looks like an ID can be forced with the "name:" prefix.

API: POST /api/v0/hosts/<id>/status, POST /api/v0/hosts/bulk-update-statuses
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl host status maintenance web-1 web-2
  mcrl host list --service web --jq '.[].id' | mcrl host status standby -

Flags:
      --no-refetch[=true|false]   print the API response ({"success": true}) instead of fetching the updated resource
```

## mcrl host update

Update a host's name, display name, memo, custom identifier, meta or checks.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl host update <host> [flags]

Update a host.

The API replaces the host's information as a whole, so the current values are
fetched and the flags (and -f fields) are applied on top; fields that are not
given keep their values. Roles are changed with "mcrl host role".
mackerel-agent overwrites meta and interfaces of hosts it runs on.

The host is given by ID, exact name, or "cid:<custom identifier>".
A name that looks like an ID can be forced with the "name:" prefix.

API: GET /api/v0/hosts/<id>, PUT /api/v0/hosts/<id>
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl host update web-1 --display-name 'Web #1' --memo 'replaced disk 2026-11'
  mcrl host update router-1 --custom-identifier ''

Flags:
      --check stringArray          check monitor name the host reports, as name or name=memo (repeatable; replaces the list)
      --custom-identifier string   custom identifier ("" clears it)
      --display-name string        display name
  -f, --file string                JSON or YAML file in the API's format ("-" for stdin); flags override its fields
      --memo string                memo
      --name string                host name
      --no-refetch[=true|false]    print the API response ({"success": true}) instead of fetching the updated resource
```
